question_text: TRAINING is to SKILL as PRACTICE is to ___?

hint_ladder.title: Hanapin ang Relationship
hint_ladder.text: Tignan ang pares: TRAINING (proseso) → SKILL (resulta). I-apply sa PRACTICE: anong resulta?

hint_ladder.title: Ano ang Direktang Resulta?
hint_ladder.text: Ang PRACTICE ay paulit-ulit na paggawa. Hindi ito teorya, libro, o exam. Ang direktang bunga? Kahusayan o MASTERY.

hint_ladder.title: Eliminahin ang Maling Choices
hint_ladder.text: A (Theory) ay bago mag-practice. C (Book) gamit lang. D (Exam) sukatan. Lahat hindi resulta. Kaya MASTERY na lang.

hint_ladder.title: Confident ka na?
hint_ladder.text: Kapag nag-practice ka ng gitara araw-araw, mastery sa kanta ang makukuha mo, hindi libro o exam. Practice leads to mastery—simple!

A.text: You might have chosen A because theory is something you study before practicing, but it's not what practice directly creates.

B.text: Correct. Practice naturally leads to mastery, mirroring how training leads to skill.

C.text: You might have chosen C because books can guide practice, but they are tools, not the outcome of practice.

D.text: You might have chosen D because practice helps you prepare for exams, but the real outcome is mastery, not just a test.

next_time_rule: Sa analogies, tanungin: 'Ano ang direktang resulta ng first word?' PRACTICE produces MASTERY, kagaya ng TRAINING produces SKILL.
deconstruct_text:
Alalahanin natin ang pagluluto ng adobo ni Lola. Ang TRAINING niya—sabi ng recipe, nanood sa YouTube—ito ang nagbigay ng SKILL. Pero ang PRACTICE, paulit-ulit na pagluluto tuwing Linggo, ang nagbunga ng MASTERY. Yung adobo niya, laging perfect ang timpla, hindi na ka...

Kaya sa analogy: TRAINING is to SKILL (cause to outcome) as PRACTICE is to MASTERY. Ganun din sa exam: pag nag-PRACTICE ka ng Civil Service reviewer, ang diretso mong makukuha ay MASTERY, hindi lang libro o exam score. Mental trick: Isipin mo ang first word ay 'makin...
